extra_quotes: A bit-exact 0.21 mm2 ASIC decoder unit (1 GHz, 7 nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to 36% and 38% (54% and 44% with prompt-lookup speculation).
the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).
Synthesis: Yosys/ABC, OpenROAD, OpenSTA, ASAP7 RVT TT, logic synthesis (pre-layout).
128 new tokens for each of 6 prompts (32 for streamed Mistral-7B on the Nano); energy integrated from the module input rail, idle included; Orin clocks pinned (MAXN SUPER).
The unit’s latency and energy are projections from measured device numbers and pre-layout synthesis, not a fabricated SoC; the FPGA shows bit- and cycle-exact decoding, but at FPGA clocks, not 1 GHz.
For streamed Mistral-7B the twin is no proxy for the unit
We did not evaluate Llama-3 or Qwen3, which quantize worse [23], or long contexts, where the uncoded fp16 KV cache dilutes the saving
